label: Institution
name: Bank of Montreal
summary:
Bank of Montreal (BMO) is Canada's oldest bank, founded in 1817 in Montreal, and one of the country's 'Big Five' banks that together control approximately 90% of Canadian banking. As Canada's first bank, BMO established the foundations of Canadian banking practice — conservative lending standards, reserve requirements, and branch banking networks that created one of the world's most stable banking systems, tested but unbroken by the 2008 global financial crisis.

BMO's founding in 1817 preceded Canadian Confederation (1867) by 50 years, making it older than Canada as a country. The bank financed the early Canadian economy: fur trade, timber exports, agricultural development, and the settlement of the Canadian West. BMO's head office moved to Toronto from Montreal in 1977, reflecting the broader economic shift from Montreal to Toronto as Canada's financial capital following Quebec's 1976 Parti Québécois election and the subsequent exodus of English Canadian businesses.

BMO's US expansion through the 2023 acquisition of Bank of the West for $16.3 billion — BMO's largest acquisition ever — extended the bank's footprint into 32 US states with 1.8 million new customers, making BMO a significant player in US banking. Canada's banking oligopoly has consistently resisted global financial crises: Canadian banks required no government bailouts in 2008, a contrast to US and European peers frequently cited as evidence of more conservative Canadian banking regulation.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bank of Montreal as Canada's oldest bank helped establish the conservative banking tradition that allowed Canadian banks to survive 2008 unscathed — one of the most cited examples of stable banking regulation in the developed world.
